name: Hushpaste secret detection rules
format: Each pattern is a JavaScript (ECMAScript) regular expression source string. Build it with new RegExp(pattern, flags).
how_to_use: Run the rules in the order listed. When two matches start at the same position, the earlier rule wins.
If a rule has a validator, keep a match only when the validator passes.
If a rule has group set to 1, the secret is capture group 1, not the whole match.
Replace each match with a placeholder such as [API_KEY_1] and keep a local map so you can restore real values later.

validators.luhn: Remove everything except digits. Require 13 to 19 digits and a valid Luhn checksum.
validators.iban_mod97: Remove spaces and uppercase. Require 15 to 34 characters. Move the first 4 characters to the end, turn letters into numbers (A=10 ... Z=35), and the resulting number modulo 97 must equal 1.
validators.ipv4_octets: Every dot-separated part must be a number from 0 to 255.

limits: Regular expressions only catch values with a recognisable shape. Names, company names, project codenames and free-text secrets are not detected, so add your own terms and review the result before sending.
license: Free to use and adapt. Provided as is, without warranty.

rules.label: Private key block
rules.notes: RSA, EC, OpenSSH, PKCS#8 and PGP private key blocks, including the lines in between. If the END line is missing, everything after the BEGIN line (up to 12,000 characters) is matched.

rules.label: Connection string with credentials
rules.notes: postgres://, mysql://, mongodb+srv://, redis://, https:// and similar URLs that contain user:password@.

rules.label: JSON Web Token
rules.notes: Three dot-separated base64url parts, the first starting with eyJ. Often a live session or access token.

rules.label: Secret API key (sk-, pk-, rk- style)
rules.notes: Covers the common sk-... style keys used by many AI and payment providers, including sk_live_ and sk_test_.

rules.label: AWS access key ID
rules.notes: Long-term (AKIA) and temporary (ASIA) access key IDs. The matching secret key is caught by SECRET.

rules.label: Slack token
rules.notes: Bot, user, app, refresh and legacy tokens (xoxb-, xoxp-, xoxa-, xoxr-, xoxs-).

rules.label: GitHub token
rules.notes: Personal, OAuth, user-to-server, server-to-server and refresh tokens, plus fine-grained tokens.

rules.label: npm access token
rules.notes: Tokens starting with npm_ followed by 36 characters.

rules.label: Secret in a URL query string
rules.notes: Only the value after the = sign is the secret (capture group 1).

rules.label: Password or secret in a key=value line
rules.notes: Catches .env lines, JSON fields and config entries such as DB_PASSWORD=..., "token": "...". Only the value (capture group 1) is the secret. May flag harmless words that follow a colon, so review matches.

rules.label: Email address
rules.notes: Common email format. Does not try to validate that the address exists.

rules.label: International phone number
rules.notes: Numbers written with a leading + and country code. Local formats without + are not detected.

rules.label: IBAN
rules.notes: With or without spaces. Run the iban_mod97 validator to drop look-alikes.

rules.label: Payment card number
rules.notes: 13 to 19 digits, optional spaces or dashes. Run the luhn validator to drop random digit strings.

rules.label: IPv4 address
rules.notes: Run the ipv4_octets validator so values such as 999.1.1.1 are ignored. Version numbers like 1.2.3.4 will still match.

rules.label: US Social Security number
rules.notes: Format 123-45-6789. Can produce false positives on other dash-separated numbers, so review matches.

performance: Patterns use bounded quantifiers so matching time grows linearly with text length, even for very long strings without spaces.
